name: Pyrite Yellow
lede: Pyrite yellow is a dark, metallic-leaning yellow named for the mineral pyrite, the iron sulfide better known as fool's gold.

sections.title: A mineral's name
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary glosses pyrite yellow simply as a dark yellow, and lists it among the yellows [1]. The mineral behind it is pyrite, which the same dictionary describes as an iron ore producing a dark brown pigment [1]. A jeweler's glossary calls pyrite a heavy, shiny, yellow mineral, also called fool's gold [2].

The Pigment Compendium treats pyrite, along with marcasite, as a naturally occurring metallic yellow iron sulfide with the formula FeS2 [3]. It also notes that an 1893 source mentions iron black as a ground iron sulfide, though it is unclear whether that came from the mineral [3]. In other words, the books give the color word and the mineral, and these sources record no tradition of painting with a pyrite-yellow paint [1][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: As a swatch, #BDA33F is a muted, slightly olive gold, the sort of tone that reads as metal rather than lemon or sunflower [4]. Nearby names include [[mustard]], [[olive]] and [[bronze]] [4]. The screen color is an approximation, not a measured mineral color [4].

notes.cite: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "pyrite", "pyrite yellow", p. 326

questions.q: What does Paterson say pyrite itself yields as a pigment?

openers: Pyrite yellow is named for fool's gold, an iron sulfide.

issues: Hedged absence claim to what the cited sources record
